events.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

args.content:
# Bookshelf

A small Next.js app for tracking what you're reading. No accounts, no database — the
books live in a single JSON file at `data/books.json`, so they survive a restart.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
```

`npm run build && npm start` for production, `npm test` for the storage tests.

## What's where

| Path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `app/page.js` | Home: currently reading, finished, and the add-book form |
| `app/books/[id]/page.js` | One book — title, author, notes, mark as finished |
| `app/actions.js` | Server actions: add, finish, save notes |
| `lib/books.js` | The JSON-file store |

# Bookshelf

A small Next.js app for tracking what you're reading. No accounts, no database — the
books live in a single JSON file at `data/books.json`, so they survive a restart.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
```

`npm run build && npm start` for production, `npm test` for the storage tests.

## What's where

| Path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `app/page.js` | Home: currently reading, finished, and the add-book form |
| `app/books/[id]/page.js` | One book — title, author, notes, mark as finished |
| `app/actions.js` | Server actions: add, finish, save notes |
| `lib/books.js` | The JSON-file store |

Every book has its own URL (`/books/<id>`) that anyone can open — that's the link you
share. Nothing is private, so don't put anything sensitive in the notes.

`data/` is gitignored: it's your shelf, not part of the code. Delete the file to start
over; back it up by copying it.

events.content:
Done. `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:3000.

**What you get**

- **Home** (`app/page.js`) — "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, plus the add-book form (title, author, optional notes). Adding drops you straight onto the new book's page.
- **Book page** (`app/books/[id]/page.js`) — title, author, notes, a "Mark as finished" button, and a copy-link button. Once finished, the button is replaced by a "Finished · <date>" tag.
- **Sharing** — each book is a plain URL like `/books/9e544397-…`. No accounts, no cookies, so anyone with the link sees the page.
- **Storage** (`lib/books.js`) — one JSON array in `data/books.json`, gitignored since it's your data.

I added one thing you didn't ask for: the notes box on the book page is editable. Notes that could only be set once, at the moment you add a book, seemed useless in practice. Say the word if you'd rather it be read-only.

**Two things worth knowing about the JSON file**, both handled but worth stating plainly since they're the usual ways a file-backed store loses data:

- Writes are serialized through a promise chain, so two near-simultaneous saves can't clobber each other (there's a test that adds 5 books at once).
- Saves write to a temp file and rename, so a crash mid-write leaves the previous version intact instead of a truncated one.

This holds for a single Next server process. It is not safe across multiple processes — if you ever deploy to something that runs several instances, or to a serverless platform with an ephemeral filesystem, this is the piece to replace with a real database.

**Verified, not just built:** `npm run build` compiles clean, and against a running production server I exercised the actual flows — added a book (persisted to disk, 303 to its page), loaded the book page cookie-less to confirm the shareable link, marked it finished (moved to the Finished list), edited notes, then killed the server and restarted it to confirm both books came back. Unknown IDs return 404. The 8 storage tests pass via `npm test`.

The forms post real HTML with hidden action fields, so add/finish/save-notes all work without JavaScript; only the copy-link button and the form's "Adding…" state need it.

curl -s http://localhost:3111/ | grep -o '<form[^>]*>.*</form>' | head -c 2000; echo; echo "=== hidden inputs ==="; curl -s http://localhost:3111/ | grep -oE '<input type="hidden"[^>]*>'

  | grep -iE '^HTTP|^x-action-redirect|^location'; echo "=== store ==="; cat data/books.json

echo "=== detail page (fresh session, no cookies) ==="
curl -s http://localhost:3111/books/$ID | grep -oE '<title>[^<]*</title>|book-title">[^<]*|book-author">[^<]*|Mark as finished|Copy link|Halls and statues[^<]*'
echo "=== finish form hidden fields ==="
curl -s http://localhost:3111/books/$ID | grep -oE '<form[^>]*>[^!]{0,400}' | head -3

ID=9e544397-33cf-41d1-a1f7-6922d1943cc0
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'finish -> HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:3111/books/$ID \

echo "=== store ==="; cat data/books.json | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>s+=d).on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(s).map(b=>[b.title,b.status,b.finishedAt])))"

ID=9e544397-33cf-41d1-a1f7-6922d1943cc0
